in_text_mentions: Pachyonychia congenita (PC, OMIM #167200 and #167210) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder of keratinization, with hallmark signs of palmoplantar keratoderma (PPK) and nail dystrophy (Fig.1). The main symptom is plantar pain. Additional characteristics include oral leucokeratosis; cysts of various types, including epidermal inclusion cysts and pilosebaceous cysts; follicular keratoses; hoarseness; hyperhidrosis; and natal teeth.
